transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Lopez (CTO - Solstice Media), Marta Ruiz (Platform Eng), Samir Patel (Dev Lead)

Summary:
Quarterly business review and health-check focused on usage trends, cost anomalies, reliability incidents in the last quarter, and roadmap alignment for Solstice's personalization pipeline. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted options, certs/audit doc requests, and next steps for a pilot benchmarking run.

Topics:
- Usage and cost trends (May -> Jun)
- Reliability incidents and error budgets
- Model and routing recommendations (batched vs low-latency routes)
- Security/compliance requests (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
- Roadmap alignment and Dedicated capacity discussion

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy to kick off the QBR. We put together a short deck, will walk usage, costs, and a couple reliability items and then open up for roadmap questions. Priya is here to help with technical bits.
[00:18] Evan Lopez: Great, thanks Alex. We appreciate the time. Quick note, Marta and Samir are dialing in from different time zones so we might jump in.
[00:28] Priya Nair: Hi all, hi Evan, hi Marta, hi Samir. Quick agenda review: usage, cost, incidents, recommendations.
[00:35] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good. We did share the recent logs and the billing CSVs earlier this week.
[00:40] Alex Chen: Yes yep we have those, thanks. I'll start with usage.
[00:45] Alex Chen: For May you were at about 18M tokens, that's up 28% month over month, mostly driven by expanded A/B tests on the recommendation model. Your per-token spend increased slightly due to more long-form generation on the low-latency tier.
[01:05] Samir Patel: That aligns with what we saw; we pushed a new personalization flow on May 7 and it did increase sequence lengths. Is there a quick way to separate cost by route?
[01:17] Alex Chen: Yes we included a per-route breakdown in the sheets. Short answer: the rec route is ~62% of cost. We can also add route tags if you want more granularity.
[01:30] Evan Lopez: We noticed a spike on May 19 with a few 5xxs, can you walk through what happened there?
[01:36] Priya Nair: Yeah there was a brief region-level outage affecting the hosted default pool. It lasted ~9 minutes and triggered automatic fallback to a cross-region route for most traffic, which increased latency for a subset of requests. The root cause was a networking flakiness in the cloud provider's region, not the model runtime itself.
[01:57] Marta Ruiz: Were logs and traces complete for that window? For audits we need preserved traces.
[02:03] Alex Chen: We have full request traces and we preserved the session logs. I'll share the trace bundle with you after the call.
[02:12] Samir Patel: Were there any token losses or truncated outputs? We saw a handful of merchant complaints about partial completions.
[02:20] Priya Nair: There were about ~120 requests that timed out due to the increased tail latency while fallback was engaging; those were retried by your client and resumed. No tokens were silently dropped by the runtime.
[02:33] Evan Lopez: Ok good. On costs, is Dedicated capacity still the primary lever to control tenant spend? We're sensitive about unit cost but also want predictable latency.
[02:44] Alex Chen: Right, Dedicated gives predictable per-token cost and lower latency tails because of pinned GPU pools. There's a tradeoff: reserved commit vs usage-based hosted. For your volume and growth, we recommended a small Dedicated pool for the rec route and keep less critical routes hosted.
[03:02] Samir Patel: Pricing question: do we get lower quantized model variants on Dedicated? i.e., if we use 4-bit quantized models can we reduce costs further?
[03:12] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated supports quantization profiles and can run int4/int8 kernels depending on model and perf tradeoffs. We also provide recommendations — we suggested QP-2 for your rec model in the slides which shows ~1.6x token cost reduction with <1% quality delta on our evals.
[03:34] Marta Ruiz: Are those evals reproducible? We need to run them against our test prompts.
[03:39] Alex Chen: Absolutely, Priya can share the eval harness and we can run a joint eval with your prompt sets.
[03:46] Priya Nair: I'll drop the harness and a script to run locally on your samples. We can also run it inside a Dedicated staging pool if you prefer.
[03:55] Evan Lopez: About security — we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS integration for keys. Anything outstanding there?
[04:03] Alex Chen: We have SOC2 Type II report available; I'll attach the PDF. We support SAML SSO for console access and KMS integration for customer-managed keys in Private deployments. For hosted, we do envelope encryption with our KMS; for Private or Dedicated we can support customer KMS/HSM.
[04:20] Marta Ruiz: Do you support audit logs for all API calls? We need per-token request logs retained for 90 days.
[04:26] Priya Nair: Yes, audit logs are available and configurable. The hosted default retention is 30 days, but we can enable extended retention as an add-on to 90 days. We'll include the cost impact in the breakout.
[04:39] Samir Patel: Great. On reliability, we'd love to lower P99 latency on the rec route — currently it's around 820ms for 1k token average. Any levers?
[04:50] Priya Nair: A few: move the rec route to Dedicated pinned pool, enable KV prefix caching for frequent prefixes (reduces compute for cached contexts), and use batching with a narrow time window for high throughput periods. We'll also tune kernel selection for your common sequence lengths.
[05:08] Alex Chen: We modeled an expected P99 improvement to ~420-480ms if you move to a small Dedicated pool + caching. We'll include those modeled numbers; real numbers will depend on your exact prompt distribution.
[05:20] Evan Lopez: That would be great. For the pilot, what's the minimum commit you'd suggest?
[05:25] Alex Chen: For the rec route volume, we recommended a 2-GPU reserved pool for the first 90-day pilot. It's a modest commit and should demonstrate both unit cost reduction and latency improvements.
[05:36] Marta Ruiz: Any additional setup work for Private vs Dedicated? Our compliance team asks about network topology.
[05:43] Priya Nair: Dedicated still uses Redwood managed control plane but offers VPC peering options and private egress. Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) is a larger effort: customer-managed control plane, on-prem package, and KMS integration. For Dedicated we can do VPC peering and restrict egress, which usually satisfies compliance teams.
[06:00] Samir Patel: On the earlier fallback incident — can we request a runbook to failover to a secondary region proactively? We want deterministic behavior on region issues.
[06:10] Alex Chen: Yes we can codify a routing policy: primary region with automatic fallback to a pre-warmed secondary region, plus canary traffic for verifying model variant compatibility. We'll prepare a draft routing policy.
[06:23] Evan Lopez: That would satisfy architecture team.
[06:26] 
[06:30] (slide change)
[06:35] Alex Chen: Now a quick look at the cost breakdown: your effective cost per 1k tokens this quarter was $0.92 on hosted; with the proposed Dedicated profile and quantization you'd see modeled cost per 1k tokens around $0.55 after committed discount and quantization. This excludes extended audit-log retention which is an add-on.
[06:55] Marta Ruiz: Is the modeled $0.55 including networking and storage?
[06:59] Alex Chen: It's compute + model serving only; we'll include networking/storage/retention as separate line items in the deck.
[07:07] Samir Patel: For our finance team, can you give a 90-day runway cost estimate under both scenarios?
[07:12] Alex Chen: Yes we'll produce a 90-day forecast for hosted-only vs hybrid Dedicated for the rec route. I'll include best/worst case based on your growth rate.
[07:21] Evan Lopez: On roadmap alignment, we plan to add multi-lingual support in Q3 and expand personalization features in Q4. Any blockers from the Redwood side?
[07:31] Priya Nair: No blockers. For multi-lingual we recommend testing model latency/quality across languages — we can help with language-specific evals. For personalization scaling, Dedicated + KV caching is the pattern we recommend.
[07:45] Marta Ruiz: For the eval harness, do you need production PII redaction? Our prompts can contain user fields.
[07:52] Alex Chen: Yes please scrub PII before sharing. We also offer an option to run evals within a staging Dedicated pool to avoid sharing real data.
[07:59] Samir Patel: For the pilot, can Redwood run a controlled benchmark against our staging traffic? We can mirror traffic.
[08:06] Priya Nair: Yes, we can coordinate a benchmark window and run with your mirrored traffic into a staging Dedicated pool. We'll need a small set of credentials and a test dataset.
[08:17] Evan Lopez: What about SLO alerting integration? We use PagerDuty.
[08:22] Alex Chen: We integrate with PagerDuty and also provide webhook-based alerting to your monitoring stack. We'll help map Redwood metrics to your alert thresholds.
[08:33] Marta Ruiz: On the SOC2 doc — can you share the latest report and also the data flow diagram?
[08:38] Alex Chen: Yes, will attach SOC2 PDF and a high-level data flow diagram showing encryption at rest, egress controls, and where customer keys are used in Private deployments.
[08:49] Samir Patel: Great. A couple of small items from our side: 1) request sample per-route cost breakdown 2) request latency distribution CSV 3) request the fallback/runbook draft.
[08:59] Alex Chen: Noted — we'll provide those.
[09:03] 
[09:07] (brief cross-talk)
[09:10] Priya Nair: Quick technical note on caching: enabling KV prefix caching requires minor prompt normalization — we can share guidelines. It tends to work well when the user prefix semantics are stable.
[09:25] Samir Patel: We'll review the guidelines and see which routes to enable caching for.
[09:30] Evan Lopez: Any blockers on committing a small Dedicated pilot this quarter?
[09:35] Alex Chen: I don't see any. The next step would be to sign a short pilot SOW and set up a 2-GPU pilot pool. We can have the SOW draft to you by 2025-06-16.
[09:48] Marta Ruiz: Who will own the SOW on Redwood side?
[09:52] Alex Chen: I'll own it (AE) and Priya will handle the technical onboarding.
[09:56] 
[10:00] (wrap-up)
[10:02] Alex Chen: Quick recap of action items and next steps: I'll send the QBR deck, SOC2, dataflow, and cost breakouts by Monday; Priya will run the benchmark and share the harness; Evan will share traces and SLOs. We'll schedule the Dedicated pilot kickoff for week of 06/23.
[10:19] Evan Lopez: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[10:22] Marta Ruiz: Thanks.
[10:24] Samir Patel: Thanks all.
[10:26] Alex Chen: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker label swaps and slight mis-hearings (e.g., 'QP-2' may appear in some places as 'QP two'). The transcript contains timestamps roughly every 20-40 seconds and preserves verbatim speech patterns including filler words.

References shared: QBR slide deck (link sent in follow-up), billing CSV (received), latency CSV (will be sent), SOC2 report (will attach), eval harness repo (link to be shared).

End of transcript.
